Redfall – A Second Chance Worth Taking

I recently reinstalled Redfall after shelving it shortly after launch, and honestly? I’m impressed. This game had a rough start—no denying that. At release, it was plagued with performance issues, lackluster AI, and just felt unfinished. Like many, I dropped it with a sense of disappointment. But curiosity got the better of me, and after hearing about a string of updates, I gave it another shot.

I’m glad I did.

After diving back in, I spent around four hours exploring the vampire-infested world of Redfall, both solo and in online co-op with friends—and I can confidently say the experience is so much smoother now. The combat feels sharp and responsive, movement is fluid, and best of all, I didn’t encounter a single crash or noticeable bug. Lag? Gone. Enemies? Actually engaging. The improvements are real.

There’s a strange satisfaction in clearing out vampire nests or teaming up to take down cultist strongholds. The atmosphere is still there—creepy yet oddly beautiful in its own way—and with the technical issues ironed out, it finally feels immersive. The servers are also still very much alive, which was a pleasant surprise, especially when jumping into co-op with minimal matchmaking issues.

Do I wish this was the version of Redfall we got at launch? Absolutely. But sometimes games need time to become what they were meant to be. It’s clear the dev team has been working hard behind the scenes to get this title into fighting shape.

If you were burned at launch, I get it—but if you still have it in your library or you’re on the fence about trying it, now might be the time to give it a second look. It’s not perfect, but it’s definitely playable—and more importantly, fun.

Played solo as Jacob – after the final patch.

Far from the most terrible game ever made, Redfall is a bog-standard, by-the-numbers looter-shooter. Too easy and not scary. PC performance is fixed though. 
5/10
Total size on my ssd: 71.8 GB

+ Performance is fixed. Redfall ran smooth and stutter-free for me (5950X +4070 Ti Super)
+ Sandbox design is great.
+ The stylized graphics are generally good. Can be degraded by excessive default brightness levels, so check that out when starting. There is a flashlight tool available throughout the game, so don’t hesitate to make things dark and use the flashlight! When you do…
+ ...The atmosphere starts to click. Darkness everywhere at night, random streetlights casting pools of light in the darkness. Even during the daytime, exploring a shed or basement will need the flashlight.

+/- enemy design is decent, but there isn’t enough variety. Barely half a dozen different vampires. The rest are human cultists or hostile mercenaries.
+/- Have seen freeze-frame cutscenes before in DLC (Just Cause 3), but they’re odd in a full game. Definitely feels like a cost-cutting measure.
+/- Story is actually decent, but feels rushed and patchy, being told through freeze-frame cutscenes w/ voiceover, collectibles, and impersonal holographs. 
+/- gameplay tries to emulate DOOM. It feels quick and slick, but movement feels a like you’re on ice-skates. Mantling / climbing works fine, but feels cumbersome in the middle of a firefight.
+/- ambient music is generally good, though there are a few odd mood choices

- First area, Redfall Commons, has a single major boss, while the second area, Burial Point, has three. Like there were plans for a larger game, but the vision for the game had to be scaled down so they jammed everything into Burial Point.
- character back-story is never explained. Jacob, for instance, has some history with one of the villains, but it’s only referenced in passing. There aren’t any collectibles which expand on it, either.
- can’t return to the first area, Redfall Commons, after leaving it
- level design is still too linear. Those times where Redfall took me out of the sandbox and into a dedicated level, the level is still a very direct path from beginning to end. 
- Too easy. You take a lot of damage, so face-tanking is out, but you also deal tons of damage. If you keep your weapons on-level and are smart with the use of cover, combat will never make you sweat.
- Not scary. Redfall’s biggest mis-step. Vampires scream, swagger and laugh, but I never felt in danger.
- Not Gothic enough. There’s a presumption that vampires = swirling cloaks, evil laughter and imposing castles with intricate spires / gargoyles and (inside) luxurious red velvet everywhere. The swirling cloaks and evil laughter are in Redfall aplenty, but the modern-day setting just didn’t work for me.
- Vram-hungry. Played at 3440x1440, max settings, and vram usage was regularly over 12GB (dedicated; allocated was even higher). I suspect some of the people complaining about stutter simply didn’t have enough vram.


Redfall is worth picking up if you can get it cheap. I had some fun clearing the map of collectibles, I didn’t hate the gameplay and it has some decent atmosphere. 100%-ing the game will require co-op; good luck finding people to play with, as the online is deserted.
